newsitem.title: USA: America's Health Network says working on new deal.
newsitem.headline: America's Health Network says working on new deal.

text.p: America's Health Network said Friday it was talking with a number of possible new investors following the recent decision by Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp to not purchase a majority interest in the television network.

The network, which leases space from Seagram Co Ltd's Universal Studios affiliate but is not financially connected to it, said it expects to complete a new transaction before the end of the month. America's Health also said it furloughed 161 employees, roughly 80 percent of its workforce, because of Columbia's very last minute decision.
"The furloughed jobs are not guaranteed at this point," said Web Golinkin, chairman and chief executive officer of America's Health Network."
"It was heartbreaking what I had to do, because our employees have gone above the call of duty. The bottom line is, these furloughs had nothing to do with AHN," he added.
The network is still on the air, running pre-recorded material.
Golinkin told Reuters the network is negotiating with several media companies but would not give specific names or the kind of investment needed to keep the cable channel on the air.
He said that right now AHN reaches 6.3 million full-time cable homes.

Golinken said that recent news reports estimated that Columbia/HCA was going invest $25 million for a majority stake in the network, but citing previous confidentiality agreements he declined to confirm or deny that figure. "Columbia pulled out at the 11th hour and 59th minute...the very the day they promised to close and fund," Golinken said. "The reasons they gave us were principally mangement changes that were imminent and the federal investigation," he added.
Probes of alleged Medicare and Medicaid fraud led to the resignations of Columbia's chairman and chief executive officer Richard Scott and president David Vandewater.
On Wednesday Three mid-level executives, at Columbia/HCA, the largest U.S. for-profit hospital company, were indicted on charges of fraud in an alleged billing scam.
A.H. Belo Corp, a media company, would relinquish its majority stake in the network when a new investor stepped in, Golinken said, adding that Belo could still hold a piece of AHN.
Golinkin said AHN currently loses money but expected to reach cash-flow breakeven in the third quarter of 1998 or 1999. He said there were no immediate plans to go public.

Other major investors, he said, included Access Health Inc and IVI Publishing Inc, an electronic publisher of interactive, multimedia health and medical information. AHN said in a statement that Allen & Co Inc, acts as the network's financial advisor as well as being an investor in the company.

"Each transaction being contemplated is quite different, so the value of the company, I guess, is in the eye of the investor. We want to find a new strategic investor, and then rethink the business plan to move forward," Golinken said. The new infusion of capital would be used to fund the network's operations and leverage its brand identity into other health care information businesses.
AHN, which launched March 25, 1996, said it receives major medical content support from the Mayo Clinic, but it doesn't have a financial stake.
